hints.title: Four Octet Segment Branching
hints.text: A valid IP address requires exactly four octets. Each octet contains one to three characters and cannot exceed integer value 255.

hints.title: Leading Zero and Range Validation
hints.text: An octet with length greater than one must not start with zero. Furthermore, its numerical value must lie between zero and 255.

hints.title: Recursive Backtracking Search
hints.text: Maintain the current index and count of formed octets. Try slice lengths of one, two, and three; recurse if valid, and collect solutions when four octets exhaust the string.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: String lengths exceeding 12 or less than 4 cannot form valid addresses and should immediately early-exit.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The search space is bounded by 3^4 = 81 total leaf evaluations, executing in strictly O(1) constant time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should check both leading zero condition and integer magnitude upper bound 255.
